groups.instruction: In each question, someone starts out facing one compass direction and then makes one or more turns. A quarter turn is 90°, a half turn is 180° and an eighth of a turn is 45°. Work out the direction they are facing at the end.
groups.example: Facing North and turning 90° clockwise gives East; turning a further 45° anticlockwise from East gives North-East.

groups.instruction: In each question, places are set out on a square grid and each one is described by how many squares it lies in a compass direction from another. A diagonal move of 3 squares means 3 squares across and 3 squares up or down. Plot the places, then work out the direction you are asked for.
groups.example: If Denby is 4 squares North of Ashford and Elmsworth is 4 squares East of Denby, then Elmsworth is 4 across and 4 up from Ashford, so Elmsworth is North-East of Ashford.

questions.stem: On a square grid, Padgate is 8 squares North-West of Kelston. Fenwick is 8 squares North-East of Padgate. Which direction is Fenwick from Kelston?
questions.explanation: Adding the legs together, Fenwick ends up 16 squares North of Kelston, so Fenwick is North of Kelston.

questions.stem: On a square grid, R is 6 squares North-West of S. T is 6 squares South of S. Q is 4 squares North-West of R. Which direction is S from Q?
questions.explanation: Plotting every point from the statements puts S 10 squares East and 10 squares South of Q, so S is South-East of Q.
